abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions (CardData, cardsForPokemon, Section, PokemonCards) are designed around the app's actual variation and stretch to new cases without copying. It stays at 4 rather than 5 because the detail-page frame is already duplicated four times and the moves data layer broke the pattern by moving into the page component.

findings.issue: Home-page card construction duplicates cardsForPokemon (app/lib/data.ts:55-69): id/name/label/sprite assembly and the species-name mapping exist twice, so card semantics changes must be made in both places and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Have the home page build its cards through a shared helper (e.g. extend cardsForPokemon or add a cardsForIndex in lib/data.ts), so card shape is defined once.

findings.issue: GameSelect rebuilds the Pokémon page URL as `?game=...`, discarding every other search param; adding any second query param to that route gets silently wiped on game change.
findings.suggestion: Read the current searchParams (via useSearchParams or the server-passed value), spread them, and override only `game` — ideally via a shared query-building helper.

findings.issue: getMoves embeds ~70 lines of fetch/transform logic in the page component, breaking the otherwise consistent pages-render / lib-data-fetches split; extending or reusing moves logic means editing or copying this page monolith.
findings.suggestion: Move getMoves (and the STAT_LABELS/METHOD_ORDER constants) into lib/data.ts next to cardsForPokemon and getSpeciesIndex, leaving the page to render.

findings.issue: Query-string construction is triplicated: Filters.href, GameSelect.tsx:23's inline template, and pageHref in app/app/page.tsx:41-49 each encode their own parameter set.
findings.suggestion: Add a small buildQuery(pathname, params) helper in lib/format.ts (it's already the shared server/client module) and use it in all three.

findings.issue: The resource detail-page frame (getX guard + generateMetadata + notFound) is copied near-verbatim in four route files (moves, abilities, types, pokemon); each new resource copies it again.
findings.suggestion: Factor a generic loader, e.g. loadResource<T>(resource, name) returning null on NotFoundError, so each page is a two-line call.

findings.issue: The em-dash MISSING constant is redefined here despite lib/format.ts:5 exporting it, and '—' also appears as a literal at app/app/moves/[name]/page.tsx:29; changing the missing-value convention touches three spots.
findings.suggestion: Import MISSING from lib/format.ts everywhere and use orMissing() for the move-page fallbacks.

findings.issue: The home page rebuilds its own type-label map with a different fallback ('' → raw name) than typeInfo/getTypeLabels (lib/data.ts:43), duplicating the label-fallback logic in a subtly different form.
findings.suggestion: Use typeInfo with getTypeLabels() like every other page, or have getTypes() return the label map the home page already consumes.

findings.issue: A synthetic ChainLink with url: "" is fabricated to satisfy the type when there is no evolution chain — a dummy API-shaped object that breaks at a distance if ChainLink grows required fields.
findings.suggestion: Handle the no-chain case in EvolutionTree (e.g. accept a fallback link or render the species link directly) instead of forging an API record.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled 60s TTL cache plus dynamic="force-dynamic" (app/app/layout.tsx:7) and fetch({cache:'no-store'}) duplicates what Next 16.4's recommended Cache Components model (cacheComponents + cacheLife/cacheTag) now provides in the framework.
findings.suggestion: Not urgent since it's confined to one module, but plan the migration when adopting future Next versions; the seams here (all fetching in api.ts) make it a contained refactor.

summary: A well-factored small app where the load-bearing abstractions (CardData, cardsForPokemon, Section, PokemonCards) genuinely absorb the app's variation, making most scenarios one-file changes: sorting cards, changing the API base URL, or removing a route are all trivial. The main drag is duplication at the seams — card assembly in two places, query-string building in three, and a four-times-copied detail-page skeleton — plus moves data logic stranded inside a page component. Fix those and this is a 5; as shipped it's a solid 4 that a new engineer could extend confidently.
